newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends lower on central bank.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends lower on central bank.

text.p: Taiwan's overnight interbank rate slid at Monday's close as recent fund injections by the central bank finally began to relieve the banking system's strapped liquidity, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate, though still in double digits, broke a string of 10 consecutive rises to finish at 10.609 percent compared to Saturday's 11.325 finish -- still roughly double the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5.
The 30-day commercial paper remained high and steady, closing at 9.50-9.75 percent against Saturday's 9.50-10.50.
The money market is closed on Tuesday for a bank holiday. It reopens on Wednesday.
The central bank, following three major liquidity injections last week, injected T$8.59 billion worth of funds into the banking system on Monday through open market operations.
Taiwan's interbank rate has persisted at double-digit levels in recent days, reflecting tight liquidity in the banking system as funds cascaded out of banks into the red-hot stock market.
In a departure from previous practice, the central bank demanded that financial institutions submit reports explaining their capital flows.
Analysts said the move aimed to prevent any of the newly released liquidity from flowing into the stock market.
Dealers said they expected the interbank rate to fall on Wednesday.
In the bond market, the benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield fell amid the fund injections.
